answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewing or renegotiating cannot meet the 18% mandate, and the contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, making deferral a supply-gap gamble rather than the benign month-to-month extension seen in memory_c5. The low-cost vendor's quote is the only option that meets the mandate alone, and memory_c2 supports a switch (sharp cost cut, quick onboarding, accurate invoicing) — but that memory predates the current constraint: the line is at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, so a wholesale cutover could convert a cost win into a delivery failure. I therefore intend a guarded switch: award primary supply to the low-cost vendor with a phased cutover and a short incumbent bridge/backup PO where terms allow, rather than a broad immediate rollover. memory_c3 (dual-sourcing removed a single point of failure) informs the bridge design. Before committing I want to verify the two load-bearing memories: memory_c2 (is the low-cost vendor's clean record real and complete?) and memory_c1 (is incumbent-stability actually as valuable as remembered, given they now refuse pricing?). Uncertainty remains on cutover execution risk at high utilization.
